cards.name: Order diamonds -> craft diamond pickaxes -> anvil Efficiency V with enderman-farm XP -> sell on /ah (DrSteve)
cards.source: videos/zJSfjgfi5Vo.txt - DrSteve, uploaded 2026-08-06 (Hindi-transliterated auto-captions of an English video; quotes below are my re-transliteration into English)
cards.claimed_profit_per_hour: 40 to 50 million profit per hour (creator extrapolates from 18 to 19 million profit in 20 to 25 minutes)
cards.capital_required: not stated; you must pre-buy diamonds and Efficiency V (books, implied) on /orders for 100+ pickaxes
cards.setup_time: enderman XP farm build (time-lapsed, duration not stated) + a small enchanting setup; enchanting the 100+ pickaxes took 15 to 20 minutes; whole cycle incl. selling 20 to 25 minutes

inputs.qty: not stated (3 per pickaxe -> 300+ for 100+ pickaxes)

inputs.item: Efficiency V (transcript says 'order Efficiency Five pickaxe'; almost certainly Efficiency V books to anvil onto the pickaxes)

outputs.unit_price: not stated (implied profit ~180k to 190k per pickaxe from 18-19M / 100+)

cards.process: 1) Build an enderman farm (End) as the XP source. 2) Build a small enchanting/anvil setup next to it. 3) Place /orders for diamonds; craft them into diamond pickaxes. 4) Place /orders for Efficiency V (books). 5) Stand at the farm, gain levels, anvil the Efficiency V book onto each pickaxe (100+ pickaxes in 15-20 minutes). 6) List every pickaxe on /ah. Creator forgot to record the selling and instead shows his auction history: 18-19M profit in 20-25 minutes. No machines beyond the enderman farm and an anvil; no AFK toggle.
tricks: Buy raw diamonds on /orders and craft the pickaxes yourself instead of buying pickaxes; buy the Efficiency V books on /orders too (both sides bought on the cheap channel, sold on the expensive channel).
Use an enderman farm as the XP source so the anvil cost of 100+ combines is free and fast (15-20 min for 100+).
Batch the whole thing: enchant 100+ pickaxes in one sitting, then dump all of them on /ah; the auction history is used as proof of sales.
Creator frames auction flipping, gambling and base raiding as the low-money methods to move away from.
quotes: [transliterated] 'today I found a method that makes over 40 to 50 million profit per hour'
[transliterated] 'to enchant this 100 plus pickaxes it took me like 15 to 20 minutes'
[transliterated] 'after selling all the pickaxes I made around 18 to 19 million profit in just like 20 to 25 minutes'
[transliterated] 'just order diamonds and convert into pickaxes and order Efficiency Five [books] and build enderman farm and just enchant pickaxes and sell it on auction house, that's it'
cards.risks: Profit figure is shown only from auction history, not recorded live; captions are auto-generated transliterations so numbers may be misheard; Efficiency V pickaxes do not stack, so 100+ listings need many /ah slot cycles (18 default) unless the creator has Donut+/++; the /ah price of Eff V pickaxes can collapse once copied; Efficiency V book supply on /orders may dry up or reprice.
cards.scalability: Bounded by Efficiency V book supply on /orders, diamond order fill speed, /ah slots (18 default, one per pickaxe, 45 Donut+, 90 Donut++) and how fast /ah buyers absorb enchanted pickaxes; XP is effectively unlimited with an enderman farm.
cards.still_valid_after_june_2026_update: yes - published 2026-08-06 (after the update); uses only /orders, /ah, a vanilla XP farm and an anvil; no /shop, no sell multiplier, no shards; re-check the current /orders price of Efficiency V books and diamonds vs the /ah price of Eff V diamond pickaxes

Batch of 100 to amortise the XP-farm trip and the listing session.

cards.name: Order Knockback I netherite swords at ~4M, resell on /ah at ~6M (KingOostin)
cards.claimed_gross_per_hour: not stated per hour; 289 mil gross from one 50-sword cycle (58 mil first batch + 231 mil second batch); 'probably played a total of 5 minutes'
cards.claimed_profit_per_hour: not stated per hour; 'almost 100 mil profit' on the cycle (289M gross - ~200M order cost = ~89M); ~2 million profit per sword
cards.capital_required: ~200 mil (50 swords x ~4 mil order price)
cards.setup_time: minutes to place the order; order filled 'in a couple hours'; AH sales took a while (checked back later)
cards.process: 1) Scan for an item with a large gap between /orders price and /ah price ('something you can sell way more than you order them for'). 2) Place a /orders buy order for 50 KB1 netherite swords at ~4M. 3) Do nothing; the order fills in a couple of hours. 4) List all 50 on /ah at ~6M. 5) Two collection rounds: 58 mil then 231 mil = 289 mil. No farms, no machines, no AFK.
tricks: Pick items with a large market gap between /orders and /ah, not the most expensive item.
Avoid ordering cheap items (bone meal, gunpowder, paper) - they cannot be resold on /ah and their prices rarely change.
Avoid super expensive items (elytra, netherite blocks, dragon heads) - their prices move millions every day, which turns the flip into investing.
Find your own item so you have less competition; he tested netherite swords, pickaxes, maces and spears before settling on KB1 netherite swords.
The specific enchant (Knockback I) is what creates the gap: cheap to fill on /orders, priced as a netherite sword on /ah.
Explicitly not: AFK skeleton spawners, AFK big farms, investing in elytra.
quotes: 'I found knockback one netherite swords to be really good as you could order them for around 4 million and sell them for around 6 million. That means you would make 2 million profit on every single netherite sword.'
'I'm going to order 50 swords'
'It looks like my order got finished in a couple hours.'
'The first time I got 58 mil and the second time I got 231 mil. That gives us a total of 289 mil which is almost 100 mil profit'
'I probably played a total of 5 minutes.'
cards.risks: Needs ~200M float; swords do not stack so 50 listings cycle through 18 /ah slots; the /orders-vs-/ah gap can close once others copy; AH sell-through is slow (two collection rounds); order may fill only partially; the ~4M/~6M numbers are from mid-August 2026.
cards.scalability: Bounded by supply of KB1 netherite swords into /orders (how many players have them to sell), /ah demand at ~6M, and /ah slots (18 default). He suggests finding your own item to avoid competition, which implies the gap is per-item and shrinks with copies.
cards.still_valid_after_june_2026_update: yes - published 2026-08-15 (after the update); pure /orders -> /ah flip; the only update effect is 18 slots instead of 25 for listing the swords

cards.name: /shop -> /orders micro-flips from a 1k start: blaze rods, shulker boxes, sweet berries (TierBlue, pre-update)
cards.source: videos/qeuCBTQwsH4.txt - TierBlue, uploaded 2025-12-30 ('100M in 1 hour using only orders' challenge, stuck in a box)
cards.claimed_gross_per_hour: challenge target 100 mil in 1 hour; actual result 134k in 1 hour from 1k start
cards.claimed_profit_per_hour: ~133k in 1 hour (134k end - 1k start); shulker box flip was the main driver ('Shulker boxes are definitely meta')
cards.capital_required: 1k starting money; scales with whatever you can buy from /shop

inputs.qty: one at a time at first

outputs.unit_price: $810 each; later 'so high' (unstated); later 'went back up to $910 each'

cards.process: 1) Open /orders and find items whose top buy order is above the /shop price. 2) Buy from /shop, fill the order ('order them away'). 3) Repeat page by page. Blaze rods gave $3 each ('only making like $6 at a time'), shulker boxes $10 each at 810 then more when the order price spiked to 910, sweet berries $20 each. Ran from 1k to 134k in the hour, mostly on shulker boxes. No machines.
tricks: Compare /orders top price against /shop price item by item; anything above shop price is a riskless fill.
Prefer items with a small unit price and big order quantity so you can buy more units per dollar (sweet berries reasoning: 'we can buy a lot more of these and make a lot more money').
Watch for order-price spikes: shulker box orders jumped from $810 to 'so high' and later $910, which made the flip pay ~100/unit instead of 10.
Order pages get exhausted ('finish out this page') and prices fall as you fill them; move to the next item.
Order books can be dropped by your own filling: quartz-block orders 'suddenly dropped down in prices' and he lost money continuing to sell.
quotes: 'Blaze rods are $153 each. Now, let me check how much they are on Slash Shop. They're $150 each.'
'Shulker boxes are $810 each, which is $10 profit.'
'Sweet berries are $51 each... We'll only make $20'
'Oh, they went back up to $910 each.'
'We made it to 134k. Shulker boxes are definitely meta'
cards.risks: Dead: /shop was removed on 2026-06-02/03, so the shop leg no longer exists. Also margins were $3-$100 per unit and the order price collapses as you fill it.
cards.scalability: Was bounded by order depth per item and click speed; irrelevant now.
cards.still_valid_after_june_2026_update: no - relies on buying from /shop, which was removed in the June 2026 update; the price-gap-scanning habit (orders vs another channel) is the only reusable part
verification_items: none for the method itself (dead); if anything, check whether any /worth sell price ever exceeds a top /orders price, which would be the post-update analogue

cards.name: Craft/smelt arbitrage inside /orders: ingots<->blocks and quartz block -> smooth quartz (TierBlue, pre-update)
cards.claimed_gross_per_hour: not stated; part of a 1k -> 134k hour; smooth quartz batch 'makes me $920', later 'should make us 4K'
cards.claimed_profit_per_hour: not stated; several of the loops were found to lose money once recomputed
cards.capital_required: 1k-13k in the video (needed 10k to try the iron-block loop; furnace 253, coal 530 x 5 = 2.65k, crafting table 90)
cards.setup_time: minutes; one furnace + crafting table ordered at 253 / 90

inputs.unit_price: 120 each (his own order placed at 176 'so it's above this raw iron'); later '200'

outputs.unit_price: 11k per block ('9.9k' for the 9 ingots, '2k per' block profit)

cards.process: Loops tried: (a) order iron ingots at 120-176, craft 9 into a block, fill the 1.5k block order (1,080 in -> 1,500 out); (b) order blocks of iron at 1.37k, uncraft to 9 ingots, fill 200-each ingot orders (1,370 in -> 1,800 out), later judged a loss after recompute; (c) order 9 gold ingots at ~1k, craft a block, fill the 11k gold-block order ('spending 10k and only making 2k per'); (d) order a furnace (253) and coal (530), craft quartz into blocks of quartz, smelt to smooth quartz, fill smooth-quartz orders ('$920', 'should make us 4K'). Machines: one furnace, one crafting table, no automation.
tricks: Place your order 1 above the current top order (iron at 176 above raw iron; furnace 253 vs 252; coal 530 vs 520) so you are 'the number one order' and get filled first.
Only price and fill orders after doing the 9x multiplication; two loops (iron block -> ingots, and a quartz loop) lost money when he skipped the math.
Smelting adds value: block of quartz -> smooth quartz sells into a separate order.
Order the tools themselves (furnace, coal, crafting table) rather than mining anything.
quotes: 'iron ingots... they are 120 each. But then if I craft them into blocks of iron, I can sell it for 1.5k each.'
'Furnaces are $252 each. So I'm going to set one for $253 each.'
'coal is $520 each. I'm going to set an order for $530 each.'
'iron blocks are 1.37k, but iron itself is 200.'
'Gold is 1k each still and 11k per block. That's 9.9k... I would be spending 10k and then only making 2k per.'
'quarts sell for $211 each... Block of quartz is $170'
cards.risks: Tiny margins, prices in the video are from Dec 2025; filling your own crafted output into orders moves the order price against you fast; several loops were net negative.
cards.scalability: Bounded by order depth on both legs and by crafting/smelting time; ~24h order lifetime.
cards.still_valid_after_june_2026_update: unknown - the mechanism (buy ingots on /orders, craft, sell blocks to /orders, or the reverse) does not depend on /shop, but every price here is pre-update and must be re-pulled; the /shop leg used for quartz blocks is gone
verification_items: current /orders prices: iron ingot, block of iron, gold ingot, gold block, quartz, block of quartz, smooth quartz
/worth for each of those (base-price floor after the sell-multiplier removal)

cards.name: AH price-history investing: candlestick patterns and a neural-net forecaster on elytra / gilded blackstone (numen)
cards.claimed_gross_per_hour: none; the trade made '$0 and probably lost some money'
cards.claimed_profit_per_hour: none; creator says 'a very small chance any of this actually works in the long term'
cards.capital_required: price of the items bought ('a few gilded blackstone off AH'); infrastructure: a server running a scraper for days
cards.setup_time: wrote a TypeScript AH-window scraper, collected ~2 days of data (later 7 days), built a React charting app, trained two models for ~2 hours each

inputs.qty: a few (plus some from his ender chest)

outputs.unit_price: not stated; did not sell ('no one wants to buy my gilded blackstone')

cards.process: 1) Get price history: either the Donut SMP API (/api gives developers a key) or a program that reads the AH window text and parses prices (he chose the scraper because the API 'seems to be inaccurate at times, and sometimes it misses a full entry'). 2) Render 5-minute candlesticks. 3) Look for bearish/bullish engulfing patterns. 4) Alternatively train a deep-learning model: 60 price points in, next 60 points out (60 points ~ 30 minutes), trained on elytra and gilded blackstone data. 5) Buy when the model says up, wait 30 minutes, relist. Result: $0.
tricks: Sellers check the cheapest listing and undercut it so their item sells first; finite items trend up because of rarity.
Candle wicks far below the close are snipes: someone lists low and it is bought instantly, then price returns.
Insider trading and price manipulation are legal on Donut SMP, so patterns are unreliable; players move prices on purpose.
Only invest when you can see a spike coming (e.g. a YouTuber about to talk about an item).
Public websites exist that show AH prices; his scraper source is on GitHub.
quotes: 'I'm going to give it 60 price points, and it will generate what it thinks will be the next 60 points.'
'I waited for 30 minutes, which was around how long 60 points was'
'I made a grand total of $0 and probably lost some money.'
'I only used like 7 days of training data, so my model isn't perfect.'
cards.risks: No edge demonstrated; illiquid items can simply not sell; manipulation is allowed; API data gaps.
cards.scalability: Data pipeline scales; the strategy did not.
cards.still_valid_after_june_2026_update: unknown - the API and price-tracking sites are infrastructure, not a method; nothing here depended on removed features, but nothing here worked either

cards.claimed_gross_per_hour: 2 shards/min with two accounts = 120 shards/h; at $3.8k per shard ~ 456k/h implied; creator frames it as 'your first 50 to 100 mil' while AFK
cards.claimed_profit_per_hour: ~$3,800 per shard via prime keys vs ~$3,000 per shard via amethyst keys

inputs.qty: 1 per minute per account (2/min with Java + Bedrock)

outputs.item: netherite helmet / netherite armor from prime key
outputs.unit_price: 5.75 mil (listed at 5.75M, sold within a couple minutes)

cards.process: AFK at /warp afk on both the Java account and its Bedrock account (2 shards/min). Go to /warp crates, open /shop -> shard shop, buy prime keys (1,500 shards) rather than amethyst keys (4,000). Math: amethyst pickaxe 12M / 4,000 = ~$3,000 per shard; 3 prime keys = 4,500 shards -> 3 x 5.75M = 17.25M -> ~$3,800 per shard. Sell the helmet on /ah at 5.75M. Side loop: hourly 'key all' gives a common crate key -> diamond armor; a full shulker of diamond helmets sells for $900,000.
tricks: Run the Java account and its Bedrock account at the same time to double AFK income.
Value crate keys per shard, not per key: prime keys beat amethyst keys ($3.8k vs $3k per shard).
Collect the hourly common key and stockpile diamond helmets into a shulker to sell as one 900k lot.

'the prime key is 1.5,000 shards and the amethyst is 4,000 shards'

cards.name: Overnight undercut buy orders on blocks/heads/gilded, hold until order prices recover (Logix method 2)
cards.claimed_gross_per_hour: not per hour; overnight positions: 1,000 diamond blocks at 29.3K (resell 50k), 1,000 emerald blocks at 14.5K (resell 25k), 32 netherite blocks at 35M (now ~41M), 32 dragon heads at 25.1M (now 32.89M), 1,000 gilded blackstone at 910,000 (now ~1.2M)
cards.claimed_profit_per_hour: not per hour; stated position profits: ~$180 million (netherite blocks), ~$250 million (dragon heads), ~$290 million (gilded); diamond/emerald blocks 'almost doubling your money'
cards.capital_required: 29.3M + 14.5M for the block orders; 1.12B for 32 netherite blocks; 803M for 32 dragon heads; 910M for 1,000 gilded ('the more money you have, the more money you can make')

outputs.unit_price: 50k each (once order prices go back up)

cards.process: Look at the /orders book for an item whose buy orders span a wide range (emerald blocks 25K to 15K, diamond blocks 50K to 30K). Place a large order at the bottom of that range (29.3K / 14.5K). Because you are undercutting, it fills overnight from sellers who need liquidity. When the order book recovers, sell to the top orders (50k / 25k). Same with 32 netherite blocks at 35M, 32 dragon heads at 25.1M, 1,000 gilded at 910K. No machines; pure balance sheet.
tricks: Place the buy order at the low end of the existing order range rather than the top; accept overnight fill in exchange for price.
Use round lots (1,000 blocks, 32 = half a stack of heads/netherite blocks).
Resell into the order book when the top order price returns, not on /ah.
Size scales with bankroll: 'the more money you have, the more money you can make off this method'.
quotes: 'emerald blocks are from like 25K to 15K... the orders are either from 50K all the way down to like 30,000'
'I'm going to order 1,000 diamond blocks at 29.3K... Emerald Block... a thousand at 14.5K'
'I placed an order for 32 Netherite blocks at 35 million each. And right now, they're going for about 41 mil. And so that's about $180 million profit.'
'I bought 32 dragon heads at 25.1 mil each. And right now they're going for 32.89. And that's about $250 million profit.'
'I placed an order for a,000 gilded at 910,000 each. And right now they're going for about 1.2 mil. And this is another $290 million profit.'
cards.risks: Capital locked overnight; ~24h order lifetime means the order may expire unfilled; prices can keep falling (KingOostin: expensive items move millions daily); Feb-2026 prices predate the June update.
cards.scalability: Scales with bankroll and with how many sellers dump into low orders overnight; bounded by 18 order slots post-update (25 before).
cards.still_valid_after_june_2026_update: unknown - mechanism (undercut orders, hold, resell to orders) survives; all prices are pre-update and the sell-multiplier removal changed base-price floors, so ranges must be re-pulled

cards.name: Order at the top of /orders, relist just under the cheapest /ah listing: dragon heads, elytra, redstone blocks, honey blocks (Logix method 3)
cards.claimed_gross_per_hour: not per hour; per flip: dragon head bought 28.4M sold 28.99M; elytra bought 282.3M sold 283.49M; redstone blocks ~165K/stack; honey blocks 'almost 900,000 a stack'
cards.claimed_profit_per_hour: not per hour; ~600k per dragon head, ~1.5M per elytra, ~20k (sometimes 100k) per stack of redstone blocks, 'over 700k' per stack of honey blocks
cards.capital_required: 'anywhere between 30 million and 300 million' for heads/elytra; redstone/honey blocks for players without hundreds of millions
cards.setup_time: minutes; orders 'delivered' quickly when placed at the top; /ah sales 'within a couple of minutes'

inputs.unit_price: 28.4 mil (orders were 'around 28.4 mil'; placed 'right below the cheapest one')

cards.process: 1) Read the top /orders price and the cheapest /ah listing for the item. 2) Place a buy order a hair above the current top order (28.4M for dragon heads; 282.3M vs 282.2M for elytra, 'make sure that it has the enchantments'). 3) When delivered, list on /ah a hair under the cheapest listing (28.99M vs 29M; 283.49M vs 284M; 164K vs 165K per stack of redstone blocks). 4) Sells within minutes. Honey blocks: order at 2.6k each and sell at almost 900k per stack.
tricks: Order placement rule: 'place an order right below the cheapest one. That way, mine gets delivered' - i.e. sit at the top of the order book by a hair so sellers hit you first.
Listing rule: 'just barely undercutting. So, mine sells first' - 28.99 vs 29, 283.49 vs 284, 164K vs 165K.
For elytra, specify the enchantments on the order so you receive a sellable one.
Stackable items (redstone blocks, honey blocks) are priced per stack on /ah but per piece on /orders; the per-stack AH price is the target.
Low-capital variant: redstone blocks (~20k per stack, sometimes 100k when an order fills cheap); honey blocks (2.6k each -> ~900k per stack).
quotes: 'I check order prices on the dragon heads and they're going for around 28.4 mil... on auction house... it's 29. So, that's easily a 600k profit.'

mechanics_facts.fact: An /orders buy order placed a little above the current top order fills instantly: buckets market 1,600, order at 1,700 'complete straight away'.
Cancelling an unfilled buy order refunds the escrowed cash: 'a load of turtle shells on order that never got fulfilled, so I think I made another 8 million just from canceling that order'.
A 50-unit order for KB1 netherite swords at ~4M 'got finished in a couple hours'.
Orders placed at the bottom of the existing order range (diamond blocks 29.3K vs 30-50K) take overnight to fill.
Orders can specify enchantments on the requested item ('make sure that it has the enchantments' on an elytra order).
Order book is price-sorted; being 'the number one order' gets you filled first; standard play is to bid 1 unit above the top order (176 vs raw iron, 253 vs 252, 530 vs 520).
Filling orders with your own output drops the order price quickly; TierBlue lost money on quartz blocks when 'they suddenly dropped down in prices'.
AH sellers check the cheapest listing and undercut it so theirs sells first; standard undercut is one tick (28.99 vs 29, 283.49 vs 284, 164K vs 165K, 46,000 vs 47,000).
AH listings expire ('if it hasn't expired before then').
Donut SMP has a public API; the /api command gives developers a key; the API 'seems to be inaccurate at times, and sometimes it misses a full entry'. Public websites also show AH prices.
Low wicks on 5-minute AH candles are instant snipes: a low listing is bought immediately and price returns.
Insider trading and price manipulation are allowed on Donut SMP; scamming is legal ('scamming is actually legal on the Donut S&P').
A Java account has a separate Bedrock account and both can be online at the same time (was used to double AFK shards).

Pre-update economy features quoted: /warp afk gave 1 shard/min; /shop had a shard shop; prime key 1,500 shards, amethyst key 4,000 shards; hourly 'key all' common crate key -> diamond armor. All removed 2026-06-02/03 (AFK shards, crates, /shop).
Pre-update /shop prices: blaze rod $150, shulker box ~$800 (order 810 = '$10 profit'), sweet berries ~$31 (order 51 = 'only make $20'). /shop removed June 2026.

Cheap bulk items (bone meal, gunpowder, paper) cannot realistically be resold on /ah and their prices rarely change; expensive items (elytra, netherite blocks, dragon heads) move by millions every day.
Auto-brewer: one turtle shell yields 3 Turtle Master potions; dropper feed order nether wart -> turtle shell -> glowstone -> gunpowder; swap the last two droppers if the hopper shows them reversed.
Auction/transaction history is viewable in-game and used as proof of sales ('I'm showing you my auction history'; 'If we look on my transactions').
Enchanting with a mob XP farm: 100+ Efficiency V pickaxes anvilled in 15-20 minutes; 100 leggings with three books each in 39 minutes.
Netherite blocks uncraft to 9 ingots, and the ingot /ah market prices separately from the block /orders market.
Stackable commodities (redstone blocks, honey blocks) trade per stack on /ah (165K, ~900K) while /orders quotes per piece (honey 2.6k).
A renewable obsidian farm is possible on the server (10-20 obsidian/s, withers involved) and sky bases with loud farms get found within an hour.
Lava buckets sold on /ah for ~20,000 each in Aug 2026 while buckets cost 1,600 on /orders.
